prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ten-frame production sprite animation for an existing illustrated desktop dog.
REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 and image 2 define ONLY the identity and drawing style: Kaifik the adult RED SHIBA INU. Image 3 is a chronological contact sheet from the user's REAL VIDEO showing a golden retriever performing a full spin. It defines MOTION AND BODY ORIENTATION ONLY, never breed, coat, ears, tail or art style.
Create a NEW ten-frame "SPIN" action of Kaifik following the physical movement in reference 3. This is a simple trained dog spinning around on short quick steps while looking up toward its handler. It is NOT chasing or looking backwards at its tail. Neck remains naturally aligned with shoulders, head turns into the direction of travel slightly before chest and pelvis, then body follows. Do not curl the dog into a C-shape. The dog's body stays anatomically straight between shoulders and hips with small natural bending as it steps. Head and neck lead the turn, no twisted backwards head. Exactly one full rotation; no back-and-forth oscillation.
IDENTITY: exactly the recognizable adult Shiba of images1-2, upright triangular ears, almond eyes, narrow fox muzzle, red/orange coat, cream muzzle/cheeks/chest/underside/feet, dark warm thin contours, detailed soft illustrated fur, curled tail attached to rump. Preserve adult long-legged slender proportions, head size and body length; no squat puppy, golden retriever features, floppy ears, long feathered tail, heavy fluffy barrel body or breed change. Match the existing 2D desktop sprite art, not photorealistic and not 3D.
LAYOUT: EXACTLY TEN separate complete full-body dogs in TWO ROWS OF FIVE equal invisible cells. Reading order is chronological left-to-right then next row, matching the TEN reference poses in image3. Wide sheet. Each dog is the same anatomical size and occupies a consistent scale within the cell, fixed floor line and fixed camera elevation slightly above the dog, as in the canonical sprite. Generous transparent margins on all sides of each dog and between dogs. No clipping, touching neighbors or tiny duplicate dogs. No text, numbers, grid or arrows.
Motion storyboard: COPY the sequence of whole-body orientations from image3:
00 body rightward, head front-right, legs slightly spread starting turn.
01 head turns toward viewer and slightly upward, chest coming frontal, forepaws begin crossing their stepping paths without tangling.
02 chest frontal, head leads toward screen LEFT with a small upward lift, shoulders pivot as one front paw makes short step.
03 LEFT-facing side/three-quarter view, chest to image LEFT, rump to image RIGHT; head follows leftward movement, no backwards glance.
04 LEFT side becoming rear-left, outer hind paw pushes off.
05 clear REAR-LEFT THREE-QUARTER, chest directed away to LEFT, head aligned with shoulders.
06 REAR view, rump toward camera, back of head visible, short hind-paw step.
07 REAR-RIGHT THREE-QUARTER, head begins looking toward screen RIGHT before torso follows.
08 rightward three-quarter body, head comes around toward viewer, paws maintain curved path.
09 RIGHT-facing near-profile, weight settles into a short next step. The next turn into 00 is small and continuous; do not repeat 00.
Paw movement: maintain weight on supporting paws, inside feet take shorter arc steps than outside feet, moderate alternating low paw lifts, legs stay anatomically attached to hips/shoulders and consistent length. Four legs total, natural occlusion allowed, no extra legs/paws, no sitting, jumping, rigid-body skating or a dog rotating with frozen legs. Tail stays curled and turns with pelvis.
All frames must remain one consistent dog, same body/head/legs scale. Smooth progression with believable lead/follow head turns. No arbitrary pose substitutions.
BACKGROUND: genuine fully transparent RGBA, opaque fur, clean antialiased silhouette. No scenery, floor, objects, cast shadows, brown gradient, checkerboard, motion effects, labels, text or props. The user needs actual usable transparent sprite cutouts.
